Folks — initial postmortem draft attached (see: 20270821-atlaspay-postmortem-draft.pdf) and a quick CSV with proposed owners (owners-action-tracker.csv). Highlights from triage:

- Root cause synopsis: two simultaneous issues — (1) a miscalibrated autoscale policy that under-provisioned a hot shard during several traffic surges, and (2) a regression in the request-routing fallback that increased cold-starts for a subset of model variants.
- Sequence: Regression deployed 07/25; traffic spike 07/28; intermittent autoscale failure 07/28–08/04; second spike 08/12 after a larger dataset rollout.

Short-term mitigations (listed in the draft):
- Force a conservative autoscale floor on the AtlasPay Dedicated pool (owner: Jonas) — immediate (<=24h).
- Emergency revert of routing change to previous stable version (owner: Rishi) — immediate (<=48h) if telemetry shows reoccurrence.
- Prefix KV warmup for hot endpoints (owner: Marissa) — 72h.

I've also included an SLA variance heatmap (sla-variance-heatmap-aug2027.xlsx) showing affected windows and estimated revenue exposure at a daily granularity.

Attachments: 20270821-atlaspay-postmortem-draft.pdf; sla-variance-heatmap-aug2027.xlsx; owners-action-tracker.csv

—Marissa

- I tested the routing rollback in staging this morning — rollout plan ready. Revert reduces p95 by ~300ms in our synthetic traffic (staging). Risk: small capacity delta at high concurrency; mitigations listed in the CSV.

- Medium-term: recommend quantization profile for model-v2 and small-model fallback on specific intents — ETA 3 weeks (performance testing + canary).
